A modification of the Bialetti Eletrikka Moka pot for precise temperature control.\nThe project uses multiple TSiC temperature sensors connected to an ESP32 microcontroller.\nA webserver running on the ESP32 provides live monitoring of temperature and heating control.
Custom PCB: Houses the ESP32 and sensor connections.
C++ Firmware (PlatformIO): Reads temperature sensors and controls the heating element.
Webserver Interface: Displays real-time temperature data via a browser.
3D-Printed Base: Designed to integrate the PCB and sensors into the machine.

A compact and precise DIY coffee scale using an ESP32 microcontroller with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. It includes a small display, touch buttons, and a web interface for configuration and live data. The scale is compatible with the “ito” espresso machine app for seamless integration.
